# Offboarding revocation

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P3 · Act as the user](../README.md#phase-3--act-as-the-user) · **Lane:** Control plane · **Label:** `feature:offboarding` · **Epic:** [#161](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/161) · **Tickets:** 7 (3S 4M)

A CP job refreshes each portal user's stored IdP refresh token on a schedule. It offboards a user only when the IdP refusal is confirmed as an upstream disable, never on token expiry, a lost rotation, a re-login or an IdP outage, and a circuit breaker pauses automatic offboarding when many users fail at once. Offboarding first contains the user (block list, API keys, sessions, cached worker tokens) and then, after a grace period, revokes provider grants and erases the user's vault entries. Admins can also offboard any user from the console.

## How we build it

- Scope and trust: the CP uses only the standard OIDC refresh_token grant against consent.oidc (the warden-portal client from W-P3-CSIG-01); Dex is never called through its own APIs. Detection depends on the upstream connector re-checking the user on refresh: the Dex LDAP connector fails a refresh only when userSearch no longer finds the user, so userSearch.filter must exclude disabled accounts, and SAML and some upstream OIDC setups never report a disabled user. In P2 require mode the ID-token and Warden-token TTLs stay the primary cutoff; offboarding adds cleanup and coverage for attribute mode.
- Config (CP-local, json:"-", never on policyWire) under consent.offboarding: mode off|observe|enforce (default off; observe classifies and alerts but never offboards), blockRetention 2160h (90 days; 0 keeps offboarding blocks forever), interval 1h (5m-24h, must stay below the IdP validIfNotUsedFor of 168h), concurrency 4, requestTimeout 10s, maxFailures 3, confirmDelay 60s, reauthWarning 72h (measured against idp_links.relink_due_at, which W-P3-CSIG-03 sets from consent.idpLink.refreshLifetime, 720h to match W-P1-DEX-01), revokeGrace 24h (automatic triggers only; manual erase is immediate), propagationWait 2m, breaker.maxPerRun 5, breaker.maxFraction 0.1. Without the consent block or --state-dir nothing is constructed and /policy is byte-identical.
- Data model: idp_links (W-P3-CSIG-03) already holds iss, sub, user_key, generation, linked_at, relink_due_at, last_refresh_at, last_refresh_status and offboarded_at. Migration idp_links/0002 adds link_state active|expiring|reauth_required|token_lost|suspect|offboarded, last_ok_at, consecutive_failures, last_error_code, rotation_pending_ref and email_verified. Migration offboarding/0001 adds offboard_runs(id, sub, iss, trigger manual|idp, actor, reason_class, stage contain|erase|done|cancelled|partial, erase_after, created_at, updated_at) with a partial unique index on sub for open runs, and offboard_steps(run_id, step, status pending|done|skipped|failed, attempts, last_error_code, updated_at). Tokens stay only in consent.store (W-P3-CSIG-06); tables hold References.
- Refresh job: started from controlplane.Server.Start next to the retention pruner, behind a Leader interface that is always-leader in SQLite mode so p5-postgres-ha can plug in its advisory lock. It runs once a minute after startup, then each sub at a hash(sub) offset inside the interval, with bounded concurrency and a run deadline of interval/2. Links whose relink_due_at has passed are skipped and marked reauth_required. For the others it reads idp/<userKey> from consent.store through LinkStore (W-P3-CSIG-03), refreshes, verifies the returned ID token (iss, aud warden-portal, sub equal to the row), sets rotation_pending_ref and writes the rotated token with LinkStore.Rotate(iss, sub, generation, token), which holds the per-user_key mutex shared with the portal callback and returns ErrStaleGeneration when a re-login won; then it updates email, email_verified and timestamps.
- Failure classification, pinned to the Dex v2.41.1 refresh responses by a contract test: 400 invalid_request 'Refresh token expired.' is expired (reauth_required, never offboard); 400 'Refresh token is invalid or has already been claimed' or any other 400 invalid_grant is token_lost (storage loss, re-login or a lost rotation; re-auth and alert, never offboard automatically); 500 invalid_request with an empty description is upstream_refused, the only automatic offboard signal, confirmed by one retry after confirmDelay and only when at least one other refresh in the run succeeded; other 5xx, 429, timeouts and network errors are transient; 401 invalid_client is config_error and pauses the job; an ID-token sub mismatch is suspect. Links within reauthWarning of relink_due_at move to expiring. token_lost users are only alerted and asked to re-authenticate; they are never offboarded automatically.
- Breaker: when confirmed candidates in one run exceed max(breaker.maxPerRun, breaker.maxFraction x active links), no automatic offboard runs; candidates are marked pending_review, a critical offboarding_paused Finding is published and an offboarding.paused audit row is written. An admin confirms or dismisses each candidate from the console. Manual offboard is never paused.
- Offboard lives in new package internal/offboard as an Offboarder built from narrow interfaces (Blocker, KeyRevoker, TokenSessionRevoker, PortalSessionRevoker, PendingCanceller, GrantRevoker, EpochBumper, SecretStore, LinkStore, Recorder, FindingPublisher) wired by internal/controlplane, so oauthbroker never imports controlplane. Steps are an ordered []Step{Name, Stage, Run} persisted in offboard_steps, so a crash resumes at the first incomplete step and p4-grants can append a step. Stage contain (immediate, reversible): BlockStore.Add({Sub, Email when verified}, actor) (W-P1-BLOCK-03; duplicate counts as done; W-P1-BLOCK-07 deletes console sessions inside Add), Server.RevokeAPIKeysForOwner(iss, sub, actor) (W-P2-APIK-03), tokensvc SessionStore.RevokeAll for (iss, sub) (W-P2-TOKX-07), delete portal_sessions for the sub (BlockStore.Add already does this through W-P3-CSIG-04, so a second call is a no-op), mark the user's open pending_authorizations denied, and EpochStore.Bump(userKey) (W-P3-PUS-08).
- Stage erase runs at erase_after (now for manual, now + revokeGrace for automatic). It waits until every live worker in WorkerRegistry reports via heartbeat a policy ETag served at or after the contain step, bounded by propagationWait. Then per grant it calls oauthbroker.RevokeUserGrant(iss, sub, provider, Actor{Kind: system}) (W-P3-PORT-02), whose retryable provider failures go to the W-P3-PORT-07 retry queue (a final failure raises provider_revoke_failed), deletes idp/<userKey> from consent.store, runs a sweep with consent.store List over secrets.UserPrefix(userKey) (W-P3-CSIG-06; a fixed-length user key plus the trailing slash, so no other user's keys can match), and sets idp_links.offboarded_at. An admin BlockStore.Remove during the grace period cancels the erase; restoring access never restores erased grants.
- Resurrection and re-entry guards: a CP refresh that raced the erase could write a rotated token back (W-P3-PUS-03 re-checks grant state, epoch and grant_id first, so this is defence in depth), so every job run re-sweeps secrets.UserPrefix(userKey) for each recently offboarded user and raises a Finding if anything was found; the W-P3-PUS-01 Vault store Delete destroys metadata and all versions (the AWS store already force-deletes). The portal callback (W-P3-CSIG-02), the portal session middleware (W-P3-CSIG-04) and /connect/start and /connect/callback (W-P3-BRKR-03, W-P3-BRKR-04) check the in-memory BlockStore snapshot and return 403 user_blocked with no idp_links, grant or consent.store write; W-P3-OFFB-06 audits and tests them together.
- Console routes, each with an authz row (W-P1-SSO-05), explicit Scope ScopeNone (W-P2-APIK-02, so no API key can offboard) and the W-P1-AAUD-02 audit middleware: GET /dashboard/api/users (admin, lists PII), POST /dashboard/api/users/{sub}/offboard {reason 1-512 bytes} returning 202 {runId} after the contain stage, GET /dashboard/api/offboard-runs/{id}, POST /dashboard/api/users/{sub}/offboard/cancel and POST /dashboard/api/offboarding/review {subs[], action confirm|dismiss}. Agents whose owner_sub (W-P2-AREG-01) is blocked or offboarded are flagged in the console and never disabled automatically.
- Audit and observability: one admin_audit row user.offboarded per run (actor system:offboarding or the console principal) with details trigger, reason_class, providers_revoked, providers_failed, api_keys_revoked, token_sessions_revoked, owned_agents and status, added to the closed details allowlist; user.offboard_cancelled on cancel. Findings go through Server.publishFinding (W-P1-OPS1-08) with the sub hashed in the DedupKey and no email: user_offboarded (high), offboarding_paused and offboarding_config_error (critical), idp_refresh_unavailable (one per issuer when most of a run is transient), idp_refresh_failing, offboarding_reauth_required, provider_revoke_failed and offboard_partial (medium). Nil-safe in-memory counters warden_cp_offboarding_refresh_total{outcome}, warden_cp_offboarding_runs_total{trigger,result} and warden_cp_offboarding_last_run_timestamp_seconds wait for W-P5-RETN-06. Logs carry only a sha256(sub) prefix and the class, never tokens, References or reasons.
- Degraded modes: CP down pauses detection and unfinished runs resume from offboard_steps on restart; IdP down gives only transient results; secret backend down still lets the contain stage finish (it needs no vault access) while refreshes and erase retry; the worker hot path changes nothing beyond the existing W-P1-BLOCK-02 block check and userGrantEpochs lookup.
- Block retention: block-list entries created by an offboard run expire automatically after consent.offboarding.blockRetention (default 90 days), keeping the list under MaxBlockedUsers (5000). An hourly sweep, which runs whenever consent and --state-dir are set regardless of mode because manual offboards also create blocks, removes only entries whose id the run's contain step recorded as created by that run (never an admin-created block) through BlockStore.Remove with actor system:offboarding, and writes one `user.offboard_block_expired` admin audit row per entry. This system expiry does not go through p2-approvals drafts; the audit row is its record.

## Done when

With consent.offboarding.mode enforce and revokeGrace 0, removing a user from an upstream directory whose connector re-checks on refresh produces, within one interval plus confirmDelay: the sub in blocked_users through BlockStore with actor system:offboarding; a 403 user_blocked from workers after their next policy poll; revoked console, portal and token-service sessions and wak_ API keys; denied pending authorizations; revoke calls at the fake Google and GitHub providers; no users/<userKey>/ or idp/<userKey> key in consent.store even after a racing refresh write-back; a refused portal login and /connect; and one user.offboarded audit row plus one user_offboarded Finding. A token past its absolute lifetime, a lost rotation, a portal re-login, IdP 5xx errors and a fleet-wide refusal never offboard anyone, and the fleet-wide case pauses automatic offboarding with a critical Finding. With the default 24h grace an admin unblock cancels the erase. Admins can offboard any sub from the console; viewers, editors and API keys get 403. Mode defaults to off, token_lost users are only alerted, and blocks created by offboarding expire after the configurable 90-day blockRetention with an audit row.

### 1/7 · W-P3-OFFB-01

**Implement the resumable two-stage Offboarder**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#162](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/162)

Add the Offboarder in new package internal/offboard that removes every credential a user holds, in two recorded stages. Contain runs at once and is reversible: block through BlockStore.Add, revoke API keys, token sessions, portal sessions and pending authorizations, and bump the user's grant epoch. Erase runs at erase_after, revokes provider grants through the shared RevokeUserGrant and then deletes the user's remaining keys in consent.store. Nothing calls it until W-P3-OFFB-03 or W-P3-OFFB-05, so merging changes no behaviour.

**Requirements**

- New internal/offboard package with `Offboarder.Offboard(ctx, Request{Sub, Iss, Reason, Actor, Trigger manual|idp, EraseAfter}) (Run, error)` built from narrow interfaces wired by internal/controlplane; internal/offboard and internal/oauthbroker never import internal/controlplane. A nil optional seam (for example token sessions disabled) records the step as skipped.
- cpstate migration offboarding/0001 adds offboard_runs and offboard_steps as in the feature design (idp_links already has iss and offboarded_at from W-P3-CSIG-03); a partial unique index allows one open run per sub. Each step is persisted before the next starts, and Server.Start calls ResumePending so open runs continue from the first incomplete step.
- Contain steps in order: BlockStore.Add({Sub, Email only when email_verified}, actor), recording on the run the entry id when this run created it (for the W-P3-OFFB-05 retention expiry), where a duplicate counts as done and records no id and the W-P1-BLOCK-07 path deletes console sessions; Server.RevokeAPIKeysForOwner(iss, sub, actor); tokensvc SessionStore.RevokeAll for (iss, sub); delete portal_sessions for the sub (PortalSessionStore.DeleteBySub from W-P3-CSIG-02, a no-op after BlockStore.Add); mark the user's open pending_authorizations denied; EpochStore.Bump(secrets.UserKey(iss, sub)) (W-P3-PUS-08). If BlockStore.Add fails (for example 422 above MaxBlockedUsers), the remaining steps still run and the run ends partial with an offboard_partial Finding.
- Erase steps in order: wait until every live worker in WorkerRegistry reports via heartbeat an ETag served at or after the contain stage, bounded by consent.offboarding.propagationWait (default 2m); oauthbroker.RevokeUserGrant(ctx, iss, sub, provider, Actor{ID: system:offboarding, Kind: system}) per active grant (W-P3-PORT-02; a retryable provider failure is parked for the W-P3-PORT-07 retry queue and a final failure raises provider_revoke_failed); delete idp/<userKey> from consent.store; sweep consent.store with List and Delete over secrets.UserPrefix(userKey); set idp_links.offboarded_at. Cancel(ctx, sub, actor) during the grace period marks the run cancelled and skips the erase.
- Keys come only from the W-P3-CSIG-06 helpers (secrets.UserKey, IdPLinkKey, UserPrefix). The user key has a fixed length and the prefix always ends with '/', so offboarding one user never touches another user's keys, whatever their subs contain.
- Idempotent: Offboard on a sub with a done run returns that run with status already_offboarded, makes no provider or store call and writes no audit row. Each finished run writes one admin_audit row user.offboarded (target users, target_ref user:<sub>, details trigger, reason_class, providers_revoked, providers_failed, api_keys_revoked, token_sessions_revoked, status) added to the closed details allowlist, and publishes user_offboarded through Server.publishFinding with DedupKey user_offboarded:<first 16 hex of sha256(sub)>.
- No token value, secrets.Ref string, email or free-text reason appears in slog or Findings; log lines carry a sha256(sub) prefix and step names only.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/offboard/offboard.go: Request, Run, Step{Name, Stage, Run}, the seam interfaces and Offboarder with Offboard, Cancel and ResumePending.
2. New internal/offboard/store.go: SQLite RunStore over offboard_runs and offboard_steps, and the cpstate migration offboarding/0001 registered next to the W-P3-CSIG-03 idp_links migration.
3. New internal/offboard/steps.go: the contain and erase step list in the order above, the erase wait over a WorkerETagSource interface, and the revoke retry with an injectable clock.
4. New internal/controlplane/offboard.go: adapters from BlockStore, Server.RevokeAPIKeysForOwner, the tokensvc SessionStore, the portal session store, the oauthbroker GrantStore and RevokeUserGrant, the W-P3-PUS-08 EpochStore, consent.store, WorkerRegistry and the adminaudit Recorder; build the Offboarder in New when --state-dir and the consent block are set and expose Server.Offboard and Server.CancelOffboard.
5. Call Offboarder.ResumePending from controlplane.Server.Start after the retention pruner goroutine starts.
6. New internal/offboard/offboard_test.go with fakes for every seam and new internal/controlplane/offboard_test.go for the wired path.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given a linked user with Google and GitHub grants, a wak_ key, a token session, a console session and a portal session, when Offboard runs with EraseAfter now, then /policy carries the sub in blockedUsers, each fake provider saw one revoke, consent.store List shows no key under users/<userKey>/ and no idp/<userKey>, the key gets 401, a token exchange gets invalid_grant/session_revoked and /auth/me with the old cookie gets 401: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestOffboard_FullRevocation`
- [ ] Given a crash hook after each step k, when the CP restarts, then the run resumes at step k+1, ends done and repeats no earlier step: `go test ./internal/offboard -run TestOffboard_Resume`
- [ ] Given a done run, when Offboard is called again, then it returns already_offboarded with no provider or SecretStore call and no new audit row: `go test ./internal/offboard -run TestOffboard_Idempotent`
- [ ] Given users with subs `abc`, `abcd` and `a/b` and stored keys for each, when `abc` is offboarded, then every key of the other two users remains: `go test ./internal/offboard -run TestOffboard_PrefixIsolation`
- [ ] Given a provider revoke returning 503, then the user's keys are still deleted, the revoke is parked for the W-P3-PORT-07 retry queue, providers_failed names the provider, the run ends partial and a provider_revoke_failed Finding is published once the retry gives up
- [ ] Given EraseAfter in 24h and a Cancel before then, then the block is gone only if the admin removed it, the run is cancelled and the fake providers saw no revoke call
- [ ] Captured logs and Findings from every test contain no token, Reference, email or reason text

### 2/7 · W-P3-OFFB-02

**Add the IdP refresh job in observe mode with safe token write-back**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#163](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/163)

Add the CP job that refreshes each portal user's stored IdP refresh token, verifies the returned ID token and writes the rotated token back without losing the chain. This ticket only observes: it records link state and alerts on outages, expiry and lost chains, and never calls Offboard. Separating it from enforcement lets operators run it safely before trusting its signal. It ships under consent.offboarding.mode, default off.

**Requirements**

- Config: ConsentOffboarding under the consent block from W-P3-CSIG-01 with strict-field registration: mode off|observe|enforce (default off), interval 1h (5m-24h), concurrency 4 (1-32), requestTimeout 10s, maxFailures 3, reauthWarning 72h (against relink_due_at from W-P3-CSIG-03). It is CP-local and never appears in GET /policy; mode enforce is accepted but behaves as observe until W-P3-OFFB-05.
- Scheduling: one goroutine from controlplane.Server.Start next to the retention pruner, behind a Leader interface (always-leader in SQLite mode); it first runs one minute after start, then refreshes each non-offboarded link at a hash(sub) offset inside the interval with bounded concurrency and a run deadline of interval/2. `RunOnce(ctx)` and an injectable clock drive tests.
- Refresh: links whose relink_due_at has passed are skipped and set to reauth_required with no refresh call. Otherwise POST grant_type=refresh_token to the token_endpoint from lazy discovery as the warden-portal client (consent.oidc.clientID and clientSecretEnv), with requestTimeout, using the token from LinkStore.Get. Verify the returned ID token iss, aud and sub against the idp_links row without a nonce; a sub mismatch sets link_state suspect and never acts. Update email and email_verified from verified claims.
- Rotation safety: set rotation_pending_ref, then write the rotated token with LinkStore.Rotate(ctx, iss, sub, generation, token) (W-P3-CSIG-03), which holds the per-user_key mutex shared with the portal callback and returns ErrStaleGeneration without writing when a re-login won. Rotate is retried up to 3 times on store errors while the token is held only in memory; rotation_pending_ref is cleared on success. If every attempt fails, set link_state token_lost and log only a sha256(sub) prefix.
- Lifetime: a link within reauthWarning of relink_due_at moves to expiring and publishes one offboarding_reauth_required Finding per user per window; a 400 'Refresh token expired.' sets reauth_required. A portal re-login (W-P3-CSIG-03 upsert) resets the link to active.
- Transient handling: transport errors, timeouts, 429 and 5xx increment consecutive_failures; at maxFailures a per-user idp_refresh_failing Finding is published only when the issuer is otherwise healthy, and one idp_refresh_unavailable Finding per issuer is published when more than half of a run is transient. 401 invalid_client publishes a critical offboarding_config_error Finding and pauses the job until restart or config reload.
- Observability: nil-safe counters warden_cp_offboarding_refresh_total{outcome} and warden_cp_offboarding_last_run_timestamp_seconds with no sub label, and one INFO line per run msg=offboarding_job_run with checked, ok, transient, expired, token_lost and duration_ms.
- Docs: a docs/control-plane.md section on the job, its config keys, the link states, and the requirement that the Dex LDAP userSearch.filter excludes disabled accounts, plus a commented userSearch.filter example in deploy/compose/dex/config.yaml (AD userAccountControl bit 2, nsAccountLock).

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/config: add ConsentOffboarding with defaults, validation and EncodeNode next to the consent block, plus a test that GET /policy never carries it.
2. Migration idp_links/0002 (new) adds link_state, last_ok_at, consecutive_failures, last_error_code, rotation_pending_ref and email_verified to idp_links (last_refresh_at and last_refresh_status already exist from W-P3-CSIG-03).
3. New internal/offboard/refresh.go: Job{Links LinkStore, Client, Verifier, Clock, Leader, Publisher} with RunOnce and Start; New internal/offboard/leader.go with Leader and AlwaysLeader.
4. New internal/offboard/tokenclient.go: refresh call returning a typed Result{Status, ErrorCode, Description, Token, IDToken}, reusing the identity ID-token verifier pattern from W-P1-SSO-03.

6. internal/controlplane: build the Job in New when the consent block, --state-dir and mode != off are set, and start it from Server.Start.
7. New internal/offboard/refresh_test.go with an httptest token endpoint and fake clock; docs/control-plane.md section.

- [ ] Given a successful refresh that returns a rotated token, then consent.store holds the new value at idp/<userKey>, generation increased and idp_links.refresh_ref equals secrets.Ref(new).String(): `go test ./internal/offboard -run TestRefreshJob_Rotation`
- [ ] Given Rotate fails 3 times on store errors, then link_state is token_lost and captured logs contain neither the token nor its Reference
- [ ] Given a portal re-login that increments generation while a refresh is in flight, then Rotate returns ErrStaleGeneration, makes no Put and the stored token is the re-login token
- [ ] Given three consecutive 503s for one user while others succeed, then one idp_refresh_failing Finding is published; given 503s for every user, then one idp_refresh_unavailable Finding is published and no per-user Finding
- [ ] Given a link 70h before relink_due_at with reauthWarning 72h, then it moves to expiring and one offboarding_reauth_required Finding is published; given a link past relink_due_at, then no refresh call is made and link_state is reauth_required
- [ ] Given mode off, then no goroutine starts and /policy is byte-identical; given mode observe, then no Offboard call is possible because the Job has no Offboarder seam: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestOffboardingJob_ModeOff`

### 3/7 · W-P3-OFFB-03

**Add the console Users tab and manual offboard routes**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#164](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/164)

Give admins a Users tab listing portal users with link state and offboarding status, and routes to offboard any sub, follow a run, cancel a pending erase and resolve breaker reviews. The offboard route runs the contain stage synchronously and returns 202, so the audit mutation lock is never held across provider calls. Every route is admin-only with Scope ScopeNone, so viewers, editors and API keys cannot offboard.

**Requirements**

- GET /dashboard/api/users (admin, because it lists emails; cursor, at most 200 per page) returns [{sub, email, linkState, linkedAt, lastRefreshAt, consecutiveFailures, reauthDueAt, grantsCount, apiKeysCount, blocked, offboardedAt, pendingReview}] with no References or token data, and also lists subs that hold only API keys or token sessions.
- POST /dashboard/api/users/{sub}/offboard {reason: 1-512 bytes, erase: bool default true} runs Offboard with the console principal as actor: 202 {runId, stage} after the contain stage; 200 {status: already_offboarded, runId}; 400 for a missing or oversized reason or invalid sub; 403 role_required for viewer and editor; 403 self_offboard_forbidden for the caller's own sub; 404 when the sub has no idp_links, grants, API keys or sessions; 503 state_dir_required without --state-dir. With erase false only the contain stage runs.
- GET /dashboard/api/offboard-runs/{id} (admin) returns the step list with status and fixed error codes, never raw provider errors. POST /dashboard/api/users/{sub}/offboard/cancel (admin) cancels an erase still in its grace period and writes user.offboard_cancelled.
- POST /dashboard/api/offboarding/review {subs[], action: confirm|dismiss} (admin) resolves breaker pending_review entries; confirm runs Offboard with the admin as actor and dismiss returns the link to active. Before W-P3-OFFB-05 the route returns 404.
- Each route has a row in the W-P1-SSO-05 authz table with Scope ScopeNone (W-P2-APIK-02), Audited:true, target users and target_ref user:<sub>; break-glass admin sessions may offboard and are recorded as breakglass:<user>. The reason is stored only in audit details and offboard_runs.
- internal/dashboard/index.html gets a Users tab (data-min-role admin) with link-state badges, offboardedAt, run progress, a pending-review list and a confirm dialog that requires typing the sub and a reason; writes go through the existing api() wrapper with X-Warden-CSRF, and the layout works at phone width.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/controlplane/users_api.go: handleUsersList, handleUserOffboard, handleOffboardRun, handleOffboardCancel and handleOffboardingReview over Server.Offboard and the offboard RunStore.
2. Register the routes in Server.Handler in internal/controlplane/controlplane.go ahead of /dashboard/ when the consent block and --state-dir are set, and add their rows to internal/controlplane/authz.go.
3. Add a users StateHasher through adminaudit RegisterStateHasher (W-P1-AAUD-02 pattern) hashing (sub, blocked, offboarded_at).
4. internal/dashboard/index.html: Users tab, run progress view and confirm dialog.
5. New internal/controlplane/users_api_test.go; document the actions in docs/control-plane.md next to the role matrix.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given viewer, editor and wak_ key principals, when they call any users route, then they get 403 and the BlockStore is unchanged: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestUsersAPI_Authz`
- [ ] Given an admin POST {reason: "left company"}, then the response is 202 with a runId, /policy carries the sub before the response returns, and one audit row has action user.offboard with the admin actor and target_ref user:<sub>
- [ ] Given an admin offboarding their own sub, then 403 self_offboard_forbidden; given an empty reason, then 400
- [ ] Given a sub with only a wak_ key and no idp_links row, when an admin offboards it, then the key is revoked and the run completes with grant steps skipped
- [ ] Given an offboarded user, then GET /dashboard/api/users shows blocked=true and offboardedAt, and the body contains no `sha256:` or token strings
- [ ] `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestAuthzRouteCoverage` passes with the new routes classified

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-OFFB-01`](offboarding.md#17--w-p3-offb-01) Implement the resumable two-stage Offboarder; [`W-P1-SSO-05`](console-sso-rbac.md#511--w-p1-sso-05) Enforce role checks on every dashboard route and replace the bearer write guard in oidc mode; [`W-P2-APIK-02`](api-keys.md#27--w-p2-apik-02) Authenticate API keys and enforce per-route scopes in the authz table

### 4/7 · W-P3-OFFB-04

**Add an E2E test for IdP-driven offboarding and its false-positive guards**

Type **test** · Size **M** · Issue [#165](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/165)

Prove the whole chain on the L1 harness (in-process CP and worker, no Docker): a user disabled upstream is blocked, their credentials revoked and their vault entries erased, and the worker denies their next request. Also prove the guards: expiry, a lost chain, a re-login and a fleet-wide refusal never offboard anyone. The default path uses the in-process fakes.OIDCIssuer with a refresh endpoint that returns the Dex v2.41.1 response shapes; a real Dex and LDAP run is an L2 subtest on the shared identity stack of W-P1-DEX-04.

**Requirements**

- New L1 scenarios in test/scenarios/offboarding.go (registered in scenarios_list.go, no build tag, no Docker): the harness starts the CP with --state-dir, a consent block pointing at fakes.OIDCIssuer (W-P1-VRFY-11, via harness.WithOIDCIssuer()), offboarding mode enforce with revokeGrace 0, fake Google and GitHub providers and fakes.MemorySecretStore as the persistent consent.store (W-P3-CSIG-06), plus a worker. Add any missing harness option in test/harness.
- Extend fakes.OIDCIssuer (W-P2-SECT-01) with a refresh_token grant and per-sub switches: Disable(sub) returns 500 {"error":"invalid_request"}, Expire(sub) returns 400 invalid_request 'Refresh token expired.' and Forget(sub) returns 400 'Refresh token is invalid or has already been claimed by another client.'. Fakes mint random token strings only.
- Happy path: link alice through /portal/login, connect Google, make one allowed worker request, Disable(alice), call RunOnce with an advanced clock past confirmDelay, then assert block list, revoke calls, vault deletion, revoked sessions and keys, a refused portal login and a worker 403 {"error":"user_blocked"} with deny event Reason=user_blocked after the next policy poll.
- Guard cases: Expire and Forget for one user never offboard; a portal re-login during a run never offboards; every user returning 500 opens the breaker with no offboard and no provider revoke; a fake racing write-back during erase is removed by the next run's re-sweep.
- L2 subtest `TestOffboardingDexRefresh` in test/e2e/identity (`//go:build e2e`, shared stack from W-P1-DEX-04, `make e2e-identity-scenario NAME=TestOffboardingDexRefresh`): delete the seeded LDAP user with ldapdelete through `docker compose exec` and log Dex's actual refresh response, so the classification table stays verified against real Dex.
- The L1 scenarios run in the default `go test -race ./...` stage of scripts/check.sh; the L2 subtest runs in the `e2e` CI job (`make e2e-identity`, W-P1-DEX-04).

**Implementation plan**

1. test/fakes/oidcissuer.go: add the refresh_token grant handler and Disable, Expire and Forget switches, with unit tests in test/fakes.
2. New test/scenarios/offboarding.go: stack setup helper and the `offboarding_disabled_user` and `offboarding_guards` scenarios.
3. Add test/e2e/identity/offboarding_dex_test.go with `TestOffboardingDexRefresh` on the stack from W-P1-DEX-04.
4. Confirm `go test ./test/scenarios` picks the scenarios up; no workflow change is needed because the default test stage already runs it.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test -race ./test/scenarios -run 'TestScenarios/offboarding_disabled_user'` passes (red first: fails before the offboarding worker exists)
- [ ] After the run the worker deny event for alice has Reason=user_blocked and the body is {"error":"user_blocked"}
- [ ] The fake Google revoke endpoint saw exactly one call and consent.store holds no key under users/<alice userKey>/ and no idp/<alice userKey>
- [ ] One user.offboarded audit row with actor system:offboarding and one user_offboarded Finding exist
- [ ] `go test -race ./test/scenarios -run 'TestScenarios/offboarding_guards'` shows no offboard for Expire, Forget and re-login, and the breaker open with an unchanged BlockStore for the fleet-wide 500 case

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-OFFB-05`](offboarding.md#57--w-p3-offb-05) Offboard on confirmed upstream refusal with a circuit breaker; [`W-P3-OFFB-03`](offboarding.md#37--w-p3-offb-03) Add the console Users tab and manual offboard routes; [`W-P3-OFFB-06`](offboarding.md#67--w-p3-offb-06) Audit and test blocked-user refusals across portal and connect; [`W-P2-SECT-01`](security-tests.md#17--w-p2-sect-01) Add security test harness with in-process CP, workers and shared fakes; [`W-P1-BLOCK-02`](user-block-list.md#212--w-p1-block-02) Enforce the block list in the worker at CONNECT and per request; [`W-P1-VRFY-11`](identity-verification.md#1112--w-p1-vrfy-11) Add the in-process OIDC issuer fake and agent token options to the test harness; [`W-P1-DEX-04`](dex-oidc.md#46--w-p1-dex-04) Add the shared L2 identity e2e stack with Dex, a CP, an attribute-mode worker and a curl agent

### 5/7 · W-P3-OFFB-05

**Offboard on confirmed upstream refusal with a circuit breaker**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#298](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/298)

Turn the observe-mode job into enforcement. A result counts as an upstream disable only when Dex reports a connector refresh failure that persists after confirmDelay while the issuer is otherwise healthy; expiry, lost chains, re-logins and outages never qualify. A per-run breaker stops automatic offboarding when too many users fail at once and leaves them for admin review. Enforcement runs only with consent.offboarding.mode enforce.

**Requirements**

- classify(link, result, runStats, now) in new internal/offboard/classify.go returns expired, token_lost, upstream_refused, transient, config_error or suspect per the feature design table, pinned by a contract test using the Dex v2.41.1 response shapes; any status the table does not know is transient.
- upstream_refused is a candidate only when a retry after consent.offboarding.confirmDelay (default 60s) gives the same result, at least one other refresh in the run succeeded, link_state is not token_lost or suspect, and rotation_pending_ref is empty.
- Breaker: when candidates exceed max(breaker.maxPerRun default 5, breaker.maxFraction default 0.1 x active links), no Offboard is called; the candidates get pending_review, a critical offboarding_paused Finding is published once per run and an offboarding.paused audit row is written.
- In mode enforce each surviving candidate calls Server.Offboard(Request{Trigger: idp, Actor: system:offboarding, Reason: upstream_refused, EraseAfter: now + revokeGrace (default 24h)}); in observe mode candidates are recorded and alerted only.
- Every run re-sweeps secrets.UserPrefix(userKey) in consent.store for users offboarded in the last 7 days, deletes anything found and publishes a medium offboard_resurrected Finding naming the provider key suffix only.
- Counter warden_cp_offboarding_runs_total{trigger,result} is added; config validation rejects maxFraction outside (0,1] and maxPerRun below 1.
- Block retention: parse consent.offboarding.blockRetention (default 2160h, 0 = never). An hourly sweep, started whenever consent and --state-dir are set (independent of mode), removes block entries recorded by a completed offboard run whose contain step finished more than blockRetention ago, through BlockStore.Remove with actor system:offboarding and one `user.offboard_block_expired` admin audit row each (outside p2-approvals drafts). Admin-created blocks never expire.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/offboard/classify.go and classify_test.go with the contract fixtures for each Dex response.
2. internal/config: add confirmDelay, revokeGrace, propagationWait and the breaker keys to ConsentOffboarding.
3. internal/offboard/refresh.go: collect candidates, schedule the confirm retry, apply the breaker, then call the Offboarder seam in enforce mode; add the re-sweep pass.
4. internal/controlplane: pass Server.Offboard into the Job when mode is enforce.
5. Extend internal/offboard/refresh_test.go with the enforcement and breaker cases.
6. internal/offboard/retention.go (new): the hourly block-retention sweep over offboard_runs with an injectable clock; internal/controlplane: start it from Server.Start when consent and --state-dir are set.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given 1 of 50 users returning 500 invalid_request on both attempts while the rest succeed, then exactly one Offboard call with reason upstream_refused: `go test ./internal/offboard -run TestEnforce_SingleRefusal`
- [ ] Given 50 of 50 users returning 500, then zero Offboard calls and no Finding other than idp_refresh_unavailable
- [ ] Given 6 of 20 users confirmed upstream_refused, then the breaker opens, zero Offboard calls happen, the 6 subs are pending_review and one critical offboarding_paused Finding is published: `go test ./internal/offboard -run TestEnforce_Breaker`
- [ ] Given 400 'Refresh token expired.' or 400 'invalid or has already been claimed', then no Offboard call and link_state is reauth_required or token_lost
- [ ] Given mode observe, then candidates are recorded and BlockStore is unchanged
- [ ] Given a racing write of users/<userKey>/google after an erase, then the next run deletes it and publishes offboard_resurrected
- [ ] With a fake clock 90 days and one hour after an offboard, the sweep removes that run's block entry, writes one user.offboard_block_expired row, and leaves an admin-created block for another user in place; with blockRetention 0 nothing is removed: `go test ./internal/offboard -run TestBlockRetention`

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-OFFB-01`](offboarding.md#17--w-p3-offb-01) Implement the resumable two-stage Offboarder; [`W-P3-OFFB-02`](offboarding.md#27--w-p3-offb-02) Add the IdP refresh job in observe mode with safe token write-back

**Unblocks:** [`W-P3-OFFB-04`](offboarding.md#47--w-p3-offb-04) Add an E2E test for IdP-driven offboarding and its false-positive guards

### 6/7 · W-P3-OFFB-06

**Audit and test blocked-user refusals across portal and connect**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#299](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/299)

An offboarded user whose IdP account still works must not sign in to the consent portal again or reconnect a provider, which would recreate idp_links, grants and consent.store entries. The checks live in their owning tickets: the portal callback (W-P3-CSIG-02), the portal session middleware (W-P3-CSIG-04), and /connect/start and /connect/callback (W-P3-BRKR-03, W-P3-BRKR-04). This ticket gives them one shared BlockChecker over the in-memory BlockStore snapshot, adds the audit rows, and proves together that a blocked sub gets 403 and nothing is written.

**Requirements**

- One adapter in internal/controlplane over the W-P1-BLOCK-07 in-memory snapshot satisfies portal.Blocklist (W-P3-CSIG-02) and oauthbroker.BlockChecker (W-P3-BRKR-03): IsBlocked(sub, email), with email matched only when verified. No handler runs a per-request SQLite query.
- Each refusal writes one admin audit row (action portal.login_denied or connect.denied, reason user_blocked) and logs only a sha256(sub) prefix; /connect/callback also marks the pending denied.
- A combined test blocks a user who has an open portal session, an open pending and a connect attempt in flight, and checks that every path returns 403 user_blocked with no portal_sessions, idp_links, oauth_grants or consent.store write.
- With an empty block list behaviour is unchanged.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/controlplane/blockchecker.go (new): the shared adapter, passed to internal/portal and internal/oauthbroker in place of per-package adapters.
2. Add the audit rows in the portal callback and the connect handlers.
3. internal/controlplane/blocked_refusal_test.go (new) for the combined case, plus unit tests in internal/portal and internal/oauthbroker with a fake BlockChecker.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given a blocked sub, when the portal callback completes, then 403 and no portal_sessions or idp_links row is created: `go test ./internal/portal -run TestCallback_BlockedUser`
- [ ] Given an open portal session whose sub is in the block snapshot but whose row was not deleted (a store fake that skips DeleteBySub), then the next /portal/api request gets 403 user_blocked
- [ ] Given a blocked sub at /connect/callback with a valid state, then 403, consent.store saw no Put and oauth_grants has no new row: `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestConnect_BlockedUser`
- [ ] `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBlockedUserRefusals` passes, and an empty block list leaves the existing portal and connect tests green

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-CSIG-04`](consent-auth.md#47--w-p3-csig-04) Add the portal session middleware, CSRF, logout and console isolation; [`W-P3-BRKR-04`](oauth-broker.md#49--w-p3-brkr-04) Implement /connect/callback and write tokens to the secret backend; [`W-P1-BLOCK-07`](user-block-list.md#712--w-p1-block-07) Deny console login and sessions for blocked principals

**Unblocks:** [`W-P3-OFFB-04`](offboarding.md#47--w-p3-offb-04) Add an E2E test for IdP-driven offboarding and its false-positive guards

### 7/7 · W-P3-OFFB-07

**Flag agents owned by blocked or offboarded users**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#300](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/300)

Registered agents keep working when their owner leaves, because owner fields are informational in P2. Show admins which agents have a blocked or offboarded owner so they can decide what to do. Offboarding never changes an agent's status on its own.

**Requirements**

- Add agentreg.Store.ListByOwner(ctx, iss, sub) to the store and the conformance suite agentregtest.Run (W-P2-AREG-01).
- GET /dashboard/api/users gains ownedAgents, and the W-P2-AREG-02 agent list gains ownerStatus active|blocked|offboarded computed from the BlockStore snapshot and idp_links.offboarded_at.
- The console Agents panel and Users tab show an owner blocked or owner offboarded badge and link to the existing admin disable action.
- Offboard adds owned_agents (count) to the user.offboarded audit details and publishes one info agent_owner_offboarded Finding per agent listing the agent id only.
- An agent's Status never changes because its owner was offboarded.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/agentreg: add ListByOwner to the Store interface, the SQLite store and agentregtest.Run.
2. internal/controlplane/users_api.go and the agent list handler: compute ownedAgents and ownerStatus.
3. internal/offboard: add an AgentLister seam used when writing the audit details and Findings.
4. internal/dashboard/index.html: badges in the Agents panel and Users tab.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given two agents owned by alice and one by bob, when alice is offboarded, then GET /dashboard/api/users shows ownedAgents=2 for alice, both agents have ownerStatus=offboarded and status active: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestAgentOwnerFlags`
- [ ] `go test ./internal/agentreg/... -run TestConformance` passes with ListByOwner covered
- [ ] One agent_owner_offboarded Finding is published per alice agent and none for bob's agent
